page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8y.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the custom Arm64-based Alibaba YiTian710 processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.75 GHz. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 64 KB L1 data cache, a 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 64 MB L3 cache. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and network performance is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.c8y.xlarge in the average tier for most general computing and memory operations. The instance achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1818.58 and a multi-core score of 7235.59. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only cached small block bandwidth of 408.75 GB/sec and an uncached large block write speed of 27.01 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, it demonstrates solid capabilities with a static web serving throughput of 6.85 GB/sec and 6.89 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. However, cryptographic and extended instruction performance is relatively weak, as indicated by a PassMark CPU encryption score of 651.04.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the custom Arm64 architecture delivers competitive performance-per-watt and resource density for workloads that do not require x86 instruction sets. Due to the lack of local storage and GPU acceleration, this instance is best suited for network-dependent, compute-bound workloads. Appropriate applications include static web serving, Redis caching layers, lightweight database operations, and basic multi-threaded data decompression tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8y.xlarge is an Arm64-based compute-optimized instance powered by a custom 2.75 GHz Alibaba YiTian710 processor. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it features 4 dedicated physical cores, 4 vCPUs, and 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance lacks local storage and GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Performance benchmarks place this server in the average tier for standard operations, highlighted by a static web serving throughput of 6.85 GB/sec and a Redis SET performance of 6.89 million operations per second. However, cryptographic performance is weak, as shown by its PassMark encryption score. This instance offers a cost-efficient profile for Arm-native workloads, making it highly suitable for web serving, caching layers, and lightweight database operations.
